paper.title: Simultaneously Learning Stochastic and Adversarial Episodic MDPs with Known Transition

settings.name_in_paper: Episodic MDP with known transition, bandit feedback, adversarial losses
unmapped: Layered episodic MDP with finite state space S and action space A, episode length L; learner picks a stochastic policy each episode
Transition function P is known to the learner (as are S, A, L)
Bandit feedback: only losses of visited state-action pairs are observed
Regret is against the best fixed policy (online linear optimisation over the occupancy-measure polytope)
settings.definition_quote: The problem of learning an episodic MDP through $T$ episodes is defined by a tuple $(S,A,P,L,\{\ell_t\}_{t=1}^T)$ ... $\ell_t: S\times A\rightarrow [0,1]$ is the loss function for episode $t$ ... with $S, A, L$, and $P$ revealed to the learner. ... The first one is the {\it adversarial setting}, where there is no assumption at all on how the losses are generated

settings.name_in_paper: Episodic MDP with known transition, losses satisfying the self-bounding condition (stochastic with corruption)
unmapped: Layered episodic MDP with finite S, A, episode length L; transition P known to the learner
Self-bounding condition: Reg_T >= E[sum_t sum_s sum_{a != pi*(s)} q_t(s,a) Delta(s,a)] - C for all q_1..q_T, with state-action gaps Delta(s,a)
settings.definition_quote: there exist a gap function $\gap: S\times A \rightarrow \fR_+$, a mapping $\pi^\star: S\rightarrow A$, and a constant $C\geq 0$ such that $\Reg_T = \E[\sum_{t=1}^T \inner{q_t - \opt, \ell_t}] \geq \E[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{s\neq s_L}\sum_{a\neq \pi^\star(s)}q_t(s,a)\gap(s,a)] - C$ holds for all sequences of $q_1, \ldots, q_T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Episodic MDP with known transition, stochastic (i.i.d.) losses
unmapped: Layered episodic MDP with finite S, A, episode length L; transition P known to the learner
Unique optimal action at every state (needed so that the gaps Delta(s,a) are positive)
settings.definition_quote: In the standard stochastic setting studied by most works in the literature, $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_T$ are i.i.d. samples of a fixed and unknown distribution.

algorithms.name: FTRL with hybrid Tsallis entropy (+ log-barrier) over occupancy measures (Algorithm 1)

source.label: col:adversarial_bound
source.quote: With $\alpha = \nicefrac{1}{\sqrt{|A|}}$, $\paralog=64L$, and $\gamma = 1$, the regret of \pref{alg:main_alg} is always bounded as $\Reg_T \leq \otil\rbr{\sqrt{L|S||A|T}}$.

results.notes: Derived from Theorem 1, whose adaptive per-episode bound is not recorded separately. The regret is defined as max over policies of E[sum of loss differences], which for an oblivious adversary is expected regret against the best fixed policy. A footnote says the result extends to adaptive adversaries. The learning rate does not depend on T, so the bound is anytime.

symbols.sum_subopt: here: sum over state-action pairs (s,a), s != s_L, a != pi*(s)
symbols.Delta_min: minimum of Delta(s,a) over s != s_L, a != pi*(s)

conditions: Condition (self-bounding constraint) holds with gap function Delta, mapping pi*, and constant C

source.label: col:stochastic_bound
source.quote: Suppose Condition~\eqref{eq:self_bounding_constraint} holds. Then with $\alpha = \nicefrac{1}{\sqrt{|A|}}$, $\paralog=64L$, and $\gamma = 1$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_alg} is bounded as $\Reg_T \leq \order(U + \sqrt{UC})$ where U = ... and $\gapmin$ is the minimal gap.

results.notes: The paper's C is the self-bounding constant. In the corruption model it equals twice the total corruption, so it maps to C_sb. The sum is over state-action pairs, not arms.

symbols.sum_subopt: here: sum over state-action pairs (s,a), s != s_L, a != pi*(s)
symbols.Delta_i: Delta(s,a) = Q(s,a) - min_{a' != a} Q(s,a') for the optimal Q function

conditions: losses i.i.d. from a fixed distribution
the optimal action at each state is unique

source.label: col:stochastic_bound
source.quote: Consequently, in the stochastic setting, we have $\Reg_T = \order(U)$.

results.notes: This is the C=0 case of Corollary 3. Appendix A.3 gives a better stochastic bound under different tuning, but it is not recorded because it appears only in the appendix text, not as a formal statement.
